changed.title: One-a-side promise: on every nonfull column an AND operand tells two row neighborhoods apart, for a graph represented by an AND/OR circuit
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (u v : Fin n)
    (j : Fin C.gates.length) (q : ℕ),
  let gate := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  let g := n + m + j.val
  let edge := fun source target : ℕ => ∃ idx : Fin C.gates.length,
    target = n + m + idx.val ∧ source ∈ (gate idx.val).inputs
  let cuts := fun (z start : ℕ) =>
    ¬ (start ≠ z ∧ C.output ≠ z ∧ Relation.ReflTransGen
      (fun prev next : ℕ => prev ≠ z ∧ next ≠ z ∧ edge prev next) start C.output)
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C → u ≠ v →
  (gate j.val).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and →
  q ∈ (gate j.val).inputs →
  cuts g u.val → cuts q v.val → ¬ Relation.ReflTransGen edge u.val q →
  ∀ c : Fin m, (∃ w : Fin n, G w c = false) →
    let col := List.replicate n false ++ List.ofFn (fun b : Fin m => decide (b = c))
    let value := (C.wires col).getD q false
    (G u c = true → value = true) ∧ (G v c = true → value = false)
changed.unlocks: one step of the count of names against literals on the one-a-side promise, which pins an AND operand at a column alone; it rests on the checked domination row and moves no bound by itself
changed.context: On paper. With only the column on, the output is off by monotonicity against a row that misses it. When adding a row changes the output, trace changed operands back to that input. For row u this path crosses the AND, so its operand q is on. Row u has no path to q, so q was on at the column alone. For row v the changed path crosses q itself. Adding the row can only turn q on, so q was off at the column alone.
